name: Exact Width of a Nested One-Coordinate Extension
statement: For $\emptyset\ne B\subseteq A\subseteq\{0,1\}^E$ and $Y=(A\times\{0\})\cup(B\times\{1\})$, one has $\sigma(Y)=\max\{\sigma(A),\sigma(B)\}$. If $B=\emptyset$, the constant-coordinate copy of $A$ has width $\sigma(A)$.
proof: Both fibers are coordinate conditionings of $Y$, giving the lower bound. Order the lower $A$ layer optimally and then the upper $B$ layer optimally. At an upper word $(b,1)$ its gate $(b,0)$ is already present, so every disagreement with the lower layer contains the singleton new-coordinate disagreement; the other minimal disagreements are precisely those from the chosen order of $B$.
